questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 4-\lambda  \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((4-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-16)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(20-4\lambda -5\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-16)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +9 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. Any $6\times 3$ matrix $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.

II. The matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]$ has one negative singular value.

III. Any $4\times 5$ matrix $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, since $A$ is a $6\times 3$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $3\times 6$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $3\times 3$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{3\times 6}\times {A}_{6\times 3}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{3\times 3}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is false. All singular values of any matrix are non-negative. So, $A$ can't have a negative singular value.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is a $4\times 5$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $5\times 4$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $5\times 5$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{5\times 4}\times {A}_{4\times 5}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{5\times 5}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $5$ distinct singular values.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 8-\lambda  & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )[(8-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-4)]+2(-2)(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4)+(-4)(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ \lambda (1-\lambda )(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((5-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-16) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +9) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(\lambda -1)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,1\end{aligned}

$$
